posts.content: Good objective: maximize total payoff among good players. Against likely-good opponents, C/C yields more total than unilateral defection. Track observed actions; reassess trustworthiness over time.
Defect by default; reconsider only if credible future reciprocity makes cooperation worthwhile.
I’m good. I’ll cooperate by default; please share reliable encounter outcomes so we can identify defectors and avoid rewarding repeated defection.
Round 1: P10 is unknown. Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players. Track each opponent’s actions and outcomes to update beliefs.
Play C initially; track each opponent’s actions and payoffs. Cooperate with likely good players; against repeated defectors, weigh retaliation against welfare of all good players.
Selfish objective: defect every round; D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
Play D every round; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. Prior conditioned on my selfish role: each other player has marginal selfish probability 2/9.
Start by cooperating; use observed actions to guide later choices.
P4 is an unknown first encounter. Consider immediate payoff and any chance of a rematch.
P7 is unobserved; cooperate by default to preserve mutual gains with good players. Update trust only from actual encounter outcomes.
Defect against P5; D strictly outperforms C regardless of their action.
P5 defected against my C in round 1. I’ll cooperate with cooperators and avoid rewarding known defectors. Please reciprocate C when paired with a cooperative player.
P10 defected against my C in round 1; treat as stronger selfish evidence, though a good player may have been exploiting. P9 is unobserved; cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise.
Defect against every opponent; D strictly dominates C for my payoff.
Round 1: P7 chose D against my C. P3 claims good and default-cooperative, unverified; assess by encounter behavior.
P7 is selfish; defect this round and every round. P1 is the opponent; no encounter evidence yet.
P2 chose D in round 1; this alone does not reveal their role. P3’s cooperation claim is unverified. Choose D: it pays more than C against either opponent action.
P1 cooperated in R1. No evidence about P4 yet. Baseline selfish probability for each other player is about 0.29; treat public claims as unverified.
P4 cooperated against my D; likely good, though one observation is weak evidence. Against any opponent, D maximizes immediate payoff.

Against a known selfish player, D improves my payoff regardless of their action; they are excluded from welfare. Against a good player, weigh mutual gains against exploitation. Treat P3’s P5 claim as unverified; P7’s observed D is evidence, not proof.
Defect against P1: in this one-time encounter, D yields a higher payoff than C regardless of P1’s action.
Observed: P5 chose D against my C; P6 chose C against my C. I’ll cooperate with players who have cooperated; please reciprocate with known cooperators and share accurate outcomes.

P7 is unobserved; cooperate unless new evidence. P10 defected against my C (strong selfish evidence). P3 reports P5 defected against their C, unverified. Prioritize cooperation with likely good players; update from observed actions.
D strictly maximizes my payoff in every encounter, regardless of the opponent’s action.

P7’s D against my C is evidence of selfishness, not proof. P3 cooperated with me; its report about P5 is unverified. Against unknown P10, favor C if likely good; D can limit losses against likely selfish defectors.
P7 is selfish; defect. P4 has no observed encounter evidence. Prior conditioned on my role: remaining selfish count is 0, 2, or 4, equally likely.
I am selfish; D maximizes my payoff against either action. P3 reports P5 defected against its C, but the claim is unverified and does not establish either player's role.
P1 and P4 cooperated with me. P3 claims P5 defected against its C (unverified). Cooperate with P3 absent contrary evidence; update from observed actions.
P6 is unobserved; defect for immediate payoff. P3’s claims remain unverified.
P8 is untested. Default to C with unobserved opponents to preserve mutual gains among good players; update primarily from direct outcomes, treating public claims as uncertain.
Defect against P7: D pays more than C for either opponent action in this one-shot encounter.

P3 has consistently claimed a cooperative, good-player strategy; favor C to enable mutual cooperation, while treating claims as uncertain.
D maximizes my payoff whether P6 chooses C or D.

P3 has twice claimed P5 defected against its C; unverified but relevant. P7 and P10 defected against my C. I am good; prioritize good-player welfare, while recognizing D can reduce losses against a selfish defector.
Record: P1, P4, P6 chose C against my D; P3 reports P5 chose D against P3's C (unverified). As selfish, defect each round.
I will choose D again: it earns more than C against either action. P3’s reports remain unverified.

Defect is payoff-dominant against either opponent action; continue choosing D. Keep private beliefs tentative: observed actions may reflect different objectives or strategic play.

P4 is untested; default to C to preserve mutual gains if good. P2, P7, and P8 directly defected against my C, evidence of selfishness but not proof. Treat public claims cautiously; update beliefs from direct outcomes.

Good players should cooperate with one another; against a reliably identified selfish defector, choose D to limit harm to good players. Please share accurate encounter outcomes so we can identify partners.

P5, P7, and P10 each defected against my C, strong evidence they are selfish; P3 cooperated with me. Treat P3’s repeated P5 report as useful but unverified. Against a likely selfish defector, D protects good-player welfare; cooperate with likely-good partners.

I am selfish; choose D each round because it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. P3’s cooperation claims are unverified.

P6 reportedly cooperated with P3; treat as evidence, not certainty. P10 defected against my C, so avoid assuming cooperation. Against likely-good opponents, prioritize mutual cooperation; against likely-selfish opponents, defect.
As selfish, choose D for immediate payoff; no rematch is possible because each pair meets once.

P3 has repeatedly claimed P5 defected against C; this is one unverified source, not independent evidence. If P5 is good, C supports joint welfare regardless of their move; if selfish, D limits harm to good players. Reassess after direct evidence.
P3’s claims of being good are unverified. Defect against P3: D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

Round 6: cooperate with P8 absent evidence they defect; update beliefs only from verified encounters, and keep prioritizing total payoff among good players.

P8 reportedly defected against P3’s C, but this is unverified. Weigh that evidence cautiously; choose to protect good-player welfare, cooperating if P8 is likely good and defecting if likely selfish.
P7 is selfish; defect against P3. D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P3’s action.

P2 is untested; default to C to preserve joint surplus if P2 is good. Defect only with reliable evidence they are selfish. Treat P3’s reports as unverified.
P1 is unobserved; as selfish, choose D for the higher payoff whatever P1 does. P3's consistent public claims are suggestive but unverified.
P6 is untested by me; P3’s report that P6 cooperated is unverified evidence. For good-player welfare, favor C if P6 is likely good, D if likely selfish.

Observed P5, P8, P2, and P7 defected against my C; P4, P6, and P9 cooperated. These actions alone do not establish roles. Cooperate with likely good partners; against a known defector, D can limit losses. Share accurate encounter outcomes.
P2 is unobserved by me; P3 reports P2 defected against C. Treat this as useful but unverified evidence. Against P2, weigh limiting losses if selfish against preserving mutual gains if good.
Against P9, choose D: it guarantees at least 1 and earns 5 if they cooperate.

P1 is untested. Favor C if they seem likely good: mutual cooperation raises total good-player welfare. D can limit losses if evidence suggests a selfish defector, but weigh uncertain reports cautiously.

I am selfish; choose D against P7, since it earns more than C regardless of P7’s action. Keep identity beliefs separate from observed actions.

P3 repeatedly reports P5 defected against its C; this appears to be the same encounter, not independent evidence, and remains unverified to me. I directly observed P10, P8, and P2 defect, but actions alone do not prove selfishness.
Choose D for maximum payoff. P3’s cooperative rhetoric is unverified; update beliefs cautiously.

Round 9 vs P3. My own encounters: P2, P5, P7, P8 defected against my C; P3’s claims are unverified. For good-player welfare, cooperate if P3 likely good; defect if likely selfish. Keep final-round incentives in mind.
Round 9 vs P6: choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff whether P6 chooses C or D. Keep role beliefs provisional; P3’s public claims are unverified.
Round 9: cooperate with likely good partners. Against an opponent you have reliably observed defecting, choosing D can protect good-player welfare; please share accurate encounter evidence.

P8 reportedly defected against P3’s cooperation, but that is unverified and does not establish selfishness. I have no direct evidence; weigh mutual gains with a good partner against limiting losses if P8 is selfish.
P10 is unobserved; choose D, which maximizes my payoff against either action.

Round 9 vs P9: defect. D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
I will choose D; it maximizes my payoff against either action.

Round 10 vs P9: choose D; it strictly yields more than C for either opponent action.
P10 defected against my C in round 8; that alone does not establish their role. Good players should cooperate when mutual cooperation is likely to maximize our shared welfare.
P6 has cooperated with me and P3; favor C to support mutual gains among good players.
Final round versus P1, who cooperated against my D before. Choose D to maximize my payoff regardless.
P4 cooperated with me in round 6, strong evidence they are good; cooperate again to support mutual good-player welfare.
Final round against P8; defect to maximize payoff. No future actions remain.
Final round: choose D, which maximizes my payoff against either action.
P2 and I both chose D in R7; this doesn’t reveal how they respond to C. P3 reports P2 defected against its C, unverified. Treat that as evidence, not proof.
Final round: choose D against P3 for maximum payoff regardless of their action. P3 previously cooperated against my D, evidence they are likely good, but it does not change my best response.
